correctness.rationale: Arbitrary generator images extend by the Leibniz rule in the exterior grading: the extension on decomposable two-vectors is well-defined by skew symmetry, on three-vectors it is the trace action, and the relations in degree four and higher are preserved. The generalized correction on three generators is x∧y∧Az, so vanishing identically is exactly A=0; this uses the characteristic assumptions and does not identify ordinary algebras by their bracket rank. For A≠0 the mixed brackets span Λ³V since (tr A)I−2A cannot vanish: its trace is tr A, then 2A=0 would follow. Projection onto Λ²V therefore leaves exactly rank b_A additional dimensions, independently of the higher generator images. Zero b_A stabilizes all lines and forces a scalar. If the nonzero image is proper, an annihilating alternating form has a radical line, and the induced operator on the two-dimensional symplectic quotient is self-adjoint and therefore scalar. Consequently A−λI has rank one. Conversely for A=λI+u⊗f, choosing a with f(a)=1 gives values on (a,a) and (a,w) for w∈ker f spanning u∧V, exactly dimension two. The rank-one translates are disjoint by the rank bound for a difference. Counting rank-one tensors modulo nonzero rescalings and multiplying by q¹² gives all three labelled counts. An independent F₅ exhaustive matrix check found 5, 0, 19220, 1933900 for ranks 0–3; it checks the matrix stratum counts, not generalized identities for all derivations.
residual_risks: Only characteristic zero and characteristic >3 as scoped. Counts are of labelled derivations, not isomorphism classes or all generalized brackets.
